findings.heading: #### F1 [MAJOR, blocking] The contract location is defined as a directory the brief passes, but three P1 commands have no such directory
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability and testability), Adzic (the acceptance check has no concrete example that passes), Cockburn (the coordinator cannot know where to look).
- Stated texts that conflict:
  - WC-4 defines the contract as `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is "the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (`S:62`). Section 2.3 repeats that the brief carries "the output directory, so the report path is known before dispatch" (`S:73`).
  - init-lite's `--output` takes a file: brief must pass `--output <file>`, report at `.dev/superclaude/context-audit.md` or `--output` (`S:87`; `INV-A:55`).
  - index-repo's brief passes nothing (`S:86`) and cleanup-audit's output directory is fixed (`.claude-audit/`, `S:85`; `INV-A:42`).
  - All three are P1 commands that must gain the contract in unattended mode (`S:159`; AC-1.1 `S:195` requires each P1 command except `load` to have a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml`).
  - AC-1.2 requires a live check on each P1 command except `load` "with `--unattended --output <dir>`" (`S:196`), and 7.2 step 4 requires `test -s <contract>` (`S:183`).
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, for init-lite, a contract at `<file passed as --output>/return-contract.yaml` (a path under a file name) or runs AC-1.2 with a directory where init-lite expects a file, and for index-repo and cleanup-audit a contract with no stated location. That is wrong because WC-4 requires the path to be known before dispatch (`S:62`), and AC-1.2 step 4 cannot be evaluated for these three commands as written.
- Not covered by the M-ids: the same location gap for later-phase commands is M2 (follow-up).
- Recommendation: state one rule for where the contract goes when the output input is a file or absent (for example the file's parent directory, or a stated flag), and make AC-1.2 name the output input per command. Priority High. Quality impact: Completeness 8 to 9, Testability 7 to 9.

findings.heading: ### R-2 [MAJOR, blocking] WC-4/WC-5/P1 scope say every command gets unattended mode and a contract; section 3.1 and AC-1.1 say brainstorm and init-lite get none
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Adzic (concrete counter-example), Fowler (count divergence).
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written leaves init-lite and brainstorm unchanged (SPEC:84, SPEC:87, SPEC:195) while the coordinator brief still passes `--unattended` from P1 on (SPEC:73) and expects a WC-4 contract from every command except `/sc:load` (SPEC:62); init-lite then writes no `return-contract.yaml`, and WC-5 tells the worker to send `--outcome failed` when "no report exists" (SPEC:63) for a run that succeeded. Two stated texts contradict each other, and AC-1.1 (SPEC:195) asserts the opposite of the P1 scope sentence (SPEC:159).
- Evidence:
  - P1 scope: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (SPEC:159) = 37 commands.
  - AC-1.1: brainstorm and init-lite "have none" (no `## Unattended mode` section), and the section is asserted on 12 commands only (SPEC:195).
  - WC-4: sole exception is `/sc:load` (SPEC:62). Init-lite's "Report today" is `context-audit.md`, "Small fix: None" (SPEC:87). Brainstorm's existing contract is only said to exist at `<output>/return-contract.yaml` (SPEC:84; INV-A:39, INV-A:97); no inventory line lists its fields, so whether it already has `command`, `artifacts`, the four-value `status` and `blocked_question` that WC-4 requires is UNVERIFIED.
  - Section 2.3 gives the coordinator no per-command rule: `--unattended` goes into every brief from P1 on, "P0 briefs omit it" (SPEC:73).
- Recommendation (Wiegers): make the three texts agree by narrowing one of them, not by adding a mechanism: either list brainstorm and init-lite as exceptions beside `/sc:load` in WC-4 and say what the worker reports for them (their existing report file), or give them the section in P1 and remove "none" from SPEC:84, SPEC:87 and SPEC:195. Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency 6 to 9.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (MAJOR, blocking) Wiegers: `/sc:load` is required to have, and not to have, a contract
findings.body:
Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text builds, for `/sc:load`, either no contract (the load row says report "none", spec:112, and Decisions says a report file "would be an unrequested addition", spec:265) or a contract (WC-4 says it is written "on every outcome" in unattended mode, spec:62; section 3 intro says every changed command gains the `## Unattended mode` section, spec:76; AC-1.1 asserts every 3.1-3.2 command has a section naming `return-contract.yaml`, spec:195), and the two cannot both hold, so AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 (spec:196, "each P1 command", which includes load by spec:159) fail against the load row as written.

Recommendation: remove load from the AC-1.1/AC-1.2 quantifier, or give load the contract; the spec's own Decisions row points to the first. Priority High.

findings.heading: ### B2 (MAJOR; Wiegers, Fowler) `/sc:load`: the per-command table and the P1 acceptance check contradict each other
findings.body:
Stated texts that contradict:

- Spec line 112 (3.2 load row): Report (WC-4) "none (see note)"; "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; Phase "P1 (usage line only)".
- Spec line 159 (P1): "`load` (usage line only)".
- Spec line 265 (Decisions): "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed."
- Spec line 195 (AC-1.1): "the test asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". `load` is in section 3.2, line 112.
- Spec line 76: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section". Line 159 also says `--unattended` is accepted "by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2", including `load`.

Wrong outcome: an implementer who does exactly what the load row and the Decisions row say (fix the Usage line only, add no report) fails AC-1.1, because the test requires an Unattended-mode section naming `return-contract.yaml` in `cmd/load.md`. An implementer who satisfies AC-1.1 adds a contract and a section to `load`, which line 265 calls an unrequested addition and line 112 says is not needed. AC-1.1 has no exception for `load`, so P1 cannot pass without breaking one of the two stated texts. Fix by naming `load` as the exception in AC-1.1, or by removing `load` from the "every command in 3.1-3.2" scope.

findings.heading: ### B4. The load row contradicts WC-4 and AC-1.1. MAJOR.
findings.body:
- Location: `SPEC:112` (load: "Report (WC-4): none"), `SPEC:265` (Decisions: a report file for load "would be an unrequested addition"), `SPEC:76` (every changed command gains the Unattended section), `SPEC:195` (AC-1.1: every command in 3.1-3.2 has a section "naming return-contract.yaml"), `SPEC:62` (WC-4: changed commands write the contract in unattended mode).
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Crispin (acceptance check).
- Wrong outcome: load is listed under "Needs a change" (`SPEC:112`), so WC-4 applies to it, but its row and its Decision say it writes no file. AC-1.1 then requires a section that names a file load never writes.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the load row and the Decision writes no contract, and that is wrong because WC-4 (`SPEC:62`) requires one for every changed command, and AC-1.1 (`SPEC:195`) fails for load without an invented section.
- Recommendation: remove load from the section 3.2 table and from AC-1.1 (it is a context loader, `SPEC:265`), or give it a contract that reports "loaded: <keys>". Pick one.
- Priority: Medium-High (small consequence, since `SPEC:112` also says load is not dispatched as its own Task). Quality impact: low to medium.

findings.heading: ### B6. `load` must write a contract (WC-4, AC-1.1, AC-1.2) but its row and decision say it writes no file
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability) and Fowler (interface).
- Location: SPEC:62 (WC-4: contract "written on every outcome" in unattended mode), SPEC:112 (load row: report "none (see note)"), SPEC:159 (P1 includes load), SPEC:195 (AC-1.1 requires `return-contract.yaml` in every section 3.1 and 3.2 command), SPEC:196 (AC-1.2 runs on each P1 command), SPEC:265 (decision: "a report file would be an unrequested addition"). INV-B:65 (load "only loads context into the current session").
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the load row writes no contract, and AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 fail for `load`; an implementer who follows WC-4 writes one, which the decision at SPEC:265 forbids, so the two texts contradict each other.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: P1 cannot pass for `load`.
- Recommendation: exempt `load` from WC-4 by name in WC-4 and in AC-1.1 and AC-1.2, or give it a one-line contract. Either way update SPEC:265.

findings.heading: ### F3. /sc:load contradicts itself on whether it names the contract. BLOCKING. MAJOR.
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Cockburn.
- Issue: The `load` row gives "Report (WC-4): none (see note)" (`spec:112`). The Decisions table says `/sc:load` gets no report file: "a report file would be an unrequested addition" (`spec:265`). AC-1.1 requires every command in 3.1-3.2 to have a section "naming `return-contract.yaml`" (`spec:195`), and `load` is in P1 (`spec:159`).
- Grading check: An implementer who follows the load row adds no contract and fails AC-1.1; an implementer who satisfies AC-1.1 writes a report file that the Decision rejects.
- Recommendation: Choose one. Either `load` writes a contract in unattended mode and the Decision at `spec:265` changes, or AC-1.1 names `load` as an explicit exception with its reason.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (blocking, MAJOR, Fowler/Hohpe): the spec-panel row describes a command surface the supplied command definition no longer has, and WC-4's contract location conflicts with it
findings.body:
Grading sentence: an implementer who follows spec:120, WC-4 (spec:62) and P2 (spec:160) adds `--output` and `--unattended` to `/sc:spec-panel` and tells the coordinator the contract is at `<--output value>.return-contract.yaml`, and that is wrong because the command definition (`command.md:22-24`) already has `--output <file>`, `--unattended`, `--report-dir`, and writes `<report-dir>/return-contract.yaml` (`command.md:460-461`), refusing the run when `--report-dir` is missing (`command.md:460`).
- The spec's basis: spec:120 ("add `--output`; contract") and spec:62 ("Where `--output` is a file (tdd, init-lite, spec-panel), the contract is `<value of --output>.return-contract.yaml`"), from INV-B:182 ("no path or `--output` flag exists (:22)") and INV-B:185.
- Contradicting source: `command.md:22-23` (usage lists `--output <file>`, `--unattended`, `--report-dir <dir>`, `--improve`), `command.md:457-465` (an Unattended mode section that points to `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, which the spec proposes to create in P0 at spec:52 and spec:158).
- Follow-on effects under the spec's own brief rule (spec:73): a brief that passes only `--output` gets a refusal printed in chat only (`command.md:460`), so no contract exists at the path WC-4 tells the coordinator to open, and AC-2.2 step 4 (spec:183, `test -s <contract>`) fails for a compliant worker. WC-4 has no rule that git-ignored paths are left out of `artifacts`, which `command.md:461` attributes to a WC-4 of the installed contract.
- Basis and limit: this holds if `command.md` is the repo's current spec-panel definition; the spec's own view of `cmd/spec-panel.md` is UNVERIFIED here. If `command.md` is current, the same staleness check is owed to every row whose basis is an inventory read dated 2026-11-02 (spec:11). Resolving evidence: diff the spec-panel row, WC-4 and the contract-location rule against the installed `WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, then decide one contract-location convention (`--report-dir` or `--output`-derived).
- Priority High. Quality impact: Consistency 4 to 8.

findings.heading: #### F-02 (BLOCKING) The spec-panel output flag conflicts with its own `--unattended` contract
findings.body:
- **Issue.** §3.2 says spec-panel gets "add `--output`; contract" (`specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:120`), and WC-4 names `--output` / `--output-dir` (`:62`). The spec-panel command already defines its unattended mode: "`--report-dir <dir>` only (`--output` is file-valued). Without it the run is refused before any work" (`command.md:460`), with the contract at `<report-dir>/return-contract.yaml` (`command.md:461`). A coordinator brief written from WC-4 for spec-panel would pass `--output` and get a refusal.
- **Grading check.** An implementer who follows §3.2 builds an `--output` flag that the command refuses under `--unattended`. Blocking: the two texts name different flags for the same contract, and the worker fails immediately.
- **Expert.** Fowler (interface), Wiegers (traceability).
- **Recommendation.** Make WC-4 name the flag per command ("`--report-dir` for spec-panel; `--output` otherwise") or adopt one name for all commands, and update §3.2's spec-panel row to match `command.md:459-461`.

findings.heading: ### B4. The `/sc:spec-panel` row (section 3.2) rests on a premise the command file contradicts
findings.body:
- Spec text: the row says `--output` must be added, that the contract must be added, that "`target_release` required as a flag for TDD inputs" (line 120), and cites `cmd/spec-panel.md:22,34-35,222,451,455`. Section 2.1 (line 52) and WC-4 (line 62) say each changed command adds one `## Unattended mode` section and that the directory flag is `--output` / `--output-dir`. `INV-B:43` states "no path or `--output` flag exists".
- Contradicting text (`command.md`, the `/sc:spec-panel` definition in the sandbox): line 23 already has `[--target-release <release>] [--output <file>] [--unattended] [--report-dir <dir>] [--improve]`. Lines 455-463 already contain a `## Unattended mode` section whose report directory is `--report-dir`, with `--output` as a file-valued flag (line 460). Line 463 already resolves the `target_release` gate as blocked.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the row adds a second `--output` flag and a second `## Unattended mode` section to a command that already has both, so the command ends with two report-path flags (`--output <file>` and `--report-dir <dir>`) and two conflicting unattended definitions, one of which WC-4 does not describe.
- Citation drift (minor, same finding): `Write` is at `command.md:224`, not 222; the Will Not line about modifying specifications is at `command.md:479`, not 451; the target-release question is at `command.md:36-37`, not 35.
- Severity: blocking, because the row's stated premise is false for the file it changes.

findings.heading: ### B2 [MAJOR, blocking] WC-4's contract location is undefined for commands whose `--output` is a file or that have no output flag, and an acceptance check depends on it
findings.body:
- Where: SPEC:62 (WC-4: "`<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)"), SPEC:87 and SPEC:90 (init-lite and tdd: `--output <file>`), SPEC:85 and SPEC:86 (cleanup-audit fixed `.claude-audit/` directory; index-repo with brief flag "none"), SPEC:200 (AC-2.2 runs `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` and requires a contract with `status: blocked`), SPEC:183 (7.2 step 4: `test -s <contract>`). A repo-wide search of the candidate finds no sentence that maps a file-valued `--output` to a contract directory.
- Grading check (PROMPTS:31): An implementer who follows WC-4 as written builds a contract at `<tdd --output value>/return-contract.yaml` (a path below a file) for tdd and init-lite, and has no coordinator-passed directory for cleanup-audit and index-repo, and that is wrong because the report path "known before dispatch" (SPEC:62) cannot be named, and AC-2.2 plus step 4 cannot pass for the tdd gate run as written. Two stated texts (WC-4 and SPEC:87,90) contradict, and an acceptance criterion cannot pass.
- Corroboration: the command definition used for this audit already separates the two, "`--report-dir <dir>` only (`--output` is file-valued)" (CMD:460); the same split is not in the spec. This is corroboration only; the spec's own evidence (SPEC:87,90) suffices.
- Expert: Cockburn (who reads the contract and from where), Newman (interface consistency), Whittaker (Zero/Empty Attack): I can break this specification by **Zero/Empty Attack**. The invariant at **SPEC:62** (report known before dispatch) fails when **the output flag is a file or missing**. Concrete attack: coordinator dispatches `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output docs/TDD_AUTH.md`; the gate resolves blocked; the command must write `docs/TDD_AUTH.md/return-contract.yaml`; `docs/TDD_AUTH.md` is not a directory and the coordinator was never told another path; `worker_done --report-path` carries nothing openable.
- Recommendation: state in WC-4, in one sentence, where the contract goes for the three shapes (directory-valued output flag, file-valued flag, no flag), or name one distinct directory flag for the contract. Rationale: the three shapes are all in section 3, so the sentence adds no new mechanism.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability +2, Completeness +1.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL as labelled by Wiegers; blocking) WC-4's file-parent rule makes parallel workers share one contract file, which WC-11 forbids
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability and consistency), Whittaker (Divergence attack, section below).
- Location: `specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:62` (WC-4), `:69` (WC-11), `:87` (init-lite `--output <file>`), `:90` (tdd `--output <file>`), `:120` (spec-panel "add `--output`"), `:73` (section 2.3), `:195-196` (AC-1.1, AC-1.2).
- Stated text: WC-4 writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` and says "when `--output` is a file, `<output-dir>` is that file's parent directory". WC-11 says "Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file."
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract written to the parent directory of each `--output <file>`, so two workers that write sibling files (two `/sc:tdd` workers with `--output docs/<domain>/TDD_A.md` and `docs/<domain>/TDD_B.md`, the default layout quoted at `inventory/commands-b.md:222`, or two `/sc:spec-panel` or `/sc:init-lite` workers with files in one folder) both write `<dir>/return-contract.yaml`, and that is wrong because WC-11 forbids two workers writing the same file and because worker A's `worker_done --report-path` then points at a file that worker B overwrote, so the coordinator reads the wrong `status`.
- This is two stated texts that contradict each other, so it is blocking. No guess about the implementer's reading is needed: the collision follows from the file-parent rule whenever two output files share a folder, and the spec's own default layout produces that. The same collision exists for this run itself (`review/audit.md` and `review/spec-panel.md` would share `review/return-contract.yaml`).
- Side effect: the contract is also dropped into tracked folders such as `docs/<domain>/`, an unrequested file in a person's tree (SA-3, `:148`).
- Recommendation (prefer narrowing): make the contract path independent of `--output` when `--output` is a file. Smallest fix: for a file-valued `--output`, name the contract `<output-file-stem>.return-contract.yaml` beside the file, or require the brief to pass a directory-valued flag for the contract. Rationale: one name per worker output removes the collision without a new mechanism. Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency +2, Testability +1.

findings.heading: ### F-1  Blocking, MAJOR (Wiegers, Whittaker): the contract location rule for a file-valued `--output` collides with the parallel-write rule
findings.body:
- Stated texts: WC-4 says that when `--output` is a file, `<output-dir>` "is that file's parent directory", and the contract is written at `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` (SPEC:62). WC-11 says "Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file" (SPEC:69).
- The spec's own briefs use file-valued `--output` for `tdd` (SPEC:90), `init-lite` (SPEC:87) and `spec-panel` (SPEC:120). The `tdd` default target is `docs/[domain]/TDD_[COMPONENT-NAME].md` (INV-B:222, `cmd/tdd.md:49` via INV-B), so sibling TDDs share a parent by default.
- Wrong outcome: an implementer who follows WC-4 as written puts the contract at the parent of the `--output` file. Two parallel `tdd` workers with `docs/auth/TDD_A.md` and `docs/auth/TDD_B.md` both write `docs/auth/return-contract.yaml`.
- The second write replaces the first, and both workers pass the same `--report-path`. If worker A ended `blocked` and B `succeeded`, the coordinator opens one file and reads B's status for A (WC-4 and 2.3 make the coordinator open that file, SPEC:62, SPEC:73).
- This is two stated texts contradicting each other, with no extra assumption beyond the spec's own model of parallel workers in one worktree (CAPS:115, SPEC:69).
- Recommendation: derive the contract name from the output file for file-valued outputs (for example `<output-file-stem>.return-contract.yaml`), or require the coordinator to give each worker its own directory and state that rule in WC-4 and 2.3.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: coordinator reads the wrong worker's status.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (MAJOR, blocking) Contract path for file-valued `--output` collides across workers
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (consistency), Whittaker (Sentinel Collision / Accumulation).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows WC-4 as written makes `/sc:tdd` and `/sc:init-lite` write `<directory containing --output>/return-contract.yaml` (`S:62`, `S:87`, `S:90`, `S:208`). That is wrong because WC-11 says two workers in one worktree must never write the same file (`S:69`): two `/sc:tdd` workers given sibling files such as `docs/tdd/auth.md` and `docs/tdd/billing.md` share `docs/tdd/return-contract.yaml`. The later write replaces the earlier worker's `status` and `blocked_question`, and the earlier worker's `worker_done --report-path` then points at another worker's report. The spec's own purpose is parallel workers, and `S:73` tells the coordinator to pass "the output directory" without saying it must be unique per worker.
- Concrete attack (Sequence/Accumulation): t0 worker A (`tdd`, `--output docs/tdd/auth.md`) writes `status: blocked`; t1 worker B (`--output docs/tdd/billing.md`) writes `status: succeeded` to the same path; t2 the coordinator opens A's `--report-path` and reads `succeeded`, while A sent `--outcome failed` (WC-5, `S:63`).
- Recommendation: narrow WC-4 for file-valued `--output` to a path that cannot be shared (either require the brief to give such a command its own dedicated directory, or name the contract after the output file's basename). Update `S:87`, `S:90` and AC-2.2 (`S:208`) to match.
- Priority High.

findings.heading: ### F-1 [MAJOR, blocking] WC-4 places the contract under "the output directory", but the brief tells tdd and spec-panel to pass a file
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (consistency), Adzic (example does not run), Whittaker (FR-2.3 sentinel/type collision: a file path used as a directory).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract at `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` with `<output-dir>` equal to the value of `--output` (`specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:62`), and for `/sc:tdd` that value is a file (`:89` "`--output <file>`", `:224` "`/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>`"), so the implementer builds `<file>/return-contract.yaml`, a path under a regular file that cannot be created, and that is wrong because AC-2.2 (`:224`) and the live check (`:199-200`, `test -s <contract>`) require a contract with `status: blocked` that does exist.
- Same defect for `/sc:spec-panel`: row `:119` says "add `--output`; contract" with no statement whether the value is a file or directory. The command text supplied for this run already defines `--output` as file-valued (`command.md:23`, `command.md:460` "`--output` is file-valued") and gives it a different contract location, `<report-dir>/return-contract.yaml` with `--report-dir` (`command.md:460-461`). WC-4 names only `--output` / `--output-dir` (`:62`). The spec resolves the file-versus-directory clash for exactly one command, init-lite (`:86`), and gives no general rule for the rest.
- Location of the failing invariant: WC-4 (`:62`) versus section 3.1 tdd row (`:89`) and section 3.2 spec-panel row (`:119`).
- Concrete attack (sentinel/type collision): brief `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output .dev/tdd/auth.md`. State before: no contract. WC-4 text says write `.dev/tdd/auth.md/return-contract.yaml`. After the TDD is written to `.dev/tdd/auth.md` the create fails, so the "written on every outcome" rule (`:62`) cannot hold for the most common outcome.
- Recommendation: state one rule in WC-4 for file-valued `--output` (for example, contract beside the file as `<file-stem>.return-contract.yaml`, or a separate required directory flag), and apply it to tdd and spec-panel in the rows.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: **B1. CRITICAL (blocking). WC-4 defines the contract location as a directory, but three commands take a file in `--output`, and AC-2.2 does so too.**
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Adzic.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract path `<--output value>/return-contract.yaml`, and that is wrong because the same spec passes a file as `--output` for these commands. Two stated texts contradict each other.
- Stated text A, spec:62: "`<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)"; the contract is `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, and the worker passes that path as `--report-path`.
- Stated text B: spec:87 (init-lite brief passes `--output <file>`), spec:90 (tdd brief passes `--output <file>`; report is "the TDD at `--output`"), spec:120 (spec-panel row says "add `--output`; contract"), spec:200 (AC-2.2 runs `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>`). The inventories agree that `--output` is a file for these (`commands-a.md:55`: `.dev/superclaude/context-audit.md` or `--output`; `commands-b.md:47`: "TDD file at `--output`").
- Concrete wrong outcome: for the tdd run of AC-2.2 the contract would be `<file>/return-contract.yaml`. On a blocked run the TDD file does not exist yet, so the command would create a directory named like the file and the next successful run could not write the TDD there. 7.2 steps 3 and 4 (spec:182-183) then check a path the spec never defines for these commands, so AC-2.2 cannot pass.
- The same ambiguity can be seen in the sibling command definition supplied with this audit: it uses `--report-dir` for the directory because `--output` is file-valued (`command.md:460-461`). That file is not part of the spec's evidence; it only shows the ambiguity is real.
- Recommendation: state one rule for the contract path when the output flag is a file (for example "the directory of that file" or a separate directory flag), and use it in WC-4, 3.1, 3.2 and AC-2.2. Priority High.

findings.heading: ### F-1 (blocking). WC-4 defines `<output-dir>` as the `--output` value, but the spec elsewhere makes `--output` a file for several commands
findings.body:
- Severity: CRITICAL. Priority: High. Expert: Wiegers (lead), Whittaker (Sentinel Collision Attack). Quality-impact estimate: Testability and Consistency each drop about 2 points.
- Whittaker form: I can break this specification by **Sentinel Collision Attack**. The invariant at **SPEC:62 (WC-4)** fails when **the caller passes a file to `--output`**. Concrete attack: coordinator brief `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output docs/TDD_AUTH.md` (the form AC-2.2 itself uses, SPEC:200). Before: no contract. WC-4 says the contract is `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` where `<output-dir>` is the directory passed as `--output`. After: the path is `docs/TDD_AUTH.md/return-contract.yaml`, which cannot be created next to a regular file. State trace: `--output` = file, contract path = child of a file, write fails or the contract lands somewhere the coordinator never learns.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract path `<--output value>/return-contract.yaml` for every command, and for tdd and init-lite that path is invalid because the spec itself says their `--output` is a file.
- Evidence of the contradiction:
  - WC-4: "where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (SPEC:62).
  - tdd row: brief passes "`--output <file>`", report today "the TDD at `--output`" (SPEC:90; INV-B:222 "TDD file at `--output`").
  - init-lite row: "`--output <file>`" (SPEC:87; INV-A:55 "`.dev/superclaude/context-audit.md` or `--output`").
  - AC-2.2 runs `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` and expects "contract `status: blocked` with a non-empty `blocked_question`" (SPEC:200). The same file-valued `--output` is implied for spec-panel, document, explain, recommend and research, whose rows say "add `--output`", "write to a file" or "explicit output" (SPEC:107-108, 115-116, 120) without saying directory or file.
  - Section 2.3 says the brief states "the output directory, so the report path is known before dispatch" (SPEC:73). For a file-valued `--output` there is no stated directory.
- Recommendation (narrow): define one rule for where the contract goes when `--output` is a file, or name a separate directory flag for the contract. Delete "`--output` / `--output-dir`" from WC-4 unless every command's `--output` is directory-valued. Restate AC-2.2 with that path.
- Reviser may touch: SPEC:62, SPEC:73 and the AC-2.2 command at SPEC:200 only.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (MAJOR, blocking) Wiegers, Adzic: the report location rule in WC-4 contradicts the rows that use a file-valued or fixed output
findings.body:
Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract at `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` for `/sc:tdd` and `/sc:init-lite`, and that is wrong because the briefs for those two pass `--output <file>` (spec:87, spec:90), so the path becomes `<file>/return-contract.yaml`, which cannot exist, and acceptance check AC-2.2 (spec:200, `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>`) then reads a contract that has no defined location.

Same defect, two more instances, all in stated text:
- WC-4 (spec:62) says the report is "known before dispatch" and sits in the directory the coordinator passed, and section 2.3 (spec:73) makes the coordinator state the output directory. The workflow row (spec:92) puts the contract at `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/return-contract.yaml`, a path the coordinator cannot know before the package exists, and the same row asks for a contract on pre-creation STOPs, when that directory does not exist yet.
- The adversarial row (spec:83) fixes the path as `<output>/adversarial/return-contract.yaml`, while WC-4 says `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`. AC-1.4 (spec:198) then tests "one fixed path" without saying which. `cleanup-audit` (spec:85) has a fixed `.claude-audit/` directory, so the coordinator cannot choose a per-run directory.

Recommendation (for the reviser, narrowest fix): state in WC-4 one rule for where the contract goes when the command's output is a file or a fixed directory, and name the exception rows (tdd, init-lite, workflow, adversarial, cleanup-audit). Priority High.

findings.heading: ### F-1 (BLOCKING, MAJOR, Wiegers/Nygard-style consistency): the fixed contract path in WC-4 contradicts WC-11 for every command that takes a file-valued `--output`
findings.body:
- Stated text: WC-4 (spec `:62`) puts a fixed-name `return-contract.yaml` "in the directory that holds the file when `--output` is a file (tdd, init-lite)"; section 3.2 does the same for spec-panel (`:120`, `INV-B:177-185`, "add `--output`"); section 3.1 repeats it for tdd and init-lite (`:87,90`). WC-11 (`:69`) says "Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file".
- Grading check: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, for tdd, init-lite and spec-panel, a `return-contract.yaml` at `dirname(--output)/return-contract.yaml`. This is wrong because two workers whose `--output` files share a directory both write that one file, so the second run overwrites the first worker's `status` and `blocked_question`, and the coordinator opens the wrong contract (a `blocked` run read as `succeeded`, or the reverse). This holds with no extra assumption: the spec's own task layout is the case, since this run's reviews are `review/spec-panel.md`, `review/disposition.md` and `review/audit.md` in one directory (README `:19-27`), and the spec never says the brief must give each file-valued `--output` its own directory. WC-11's carve-out (timestamp or slug in default paths) covers default report paths, not the contract name, and section 3.1 handles the same hazard for cleanup-audit only (`:85`, "one audit per worktree").
- Expert: Wiegers (requirement consistency), Whittaker (FR-2.4 sequence/accumulation: the shared file is overwritten).
- Recommendation: either name the contract per output (for example `<output-stem>.return-contract.yaml`) for file-valued `--output`, or add to section 2.3 and WC-4 that a file-valued `--output` must sit in a directory no other worker uses. Narrowing beats adding.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: coordinator reads of worker status become unreliable under parallel dispatch, the headline use of the design.

findings.heading: ### F-2 [BLOCKING] [MAJOR] WC-4's fixed-name contract in "the directory that holds the file" collides for sibling outputs, which WC-11 forbids
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers, Adzic (concrete scenario), Whittaker (Accumulation attack).
- Stated texts: WC-4 `spec:62`: the report directory is "the directory that holds the file when `--output` is a file (tdd, init-lite)", and the file is always `return-contract.yaml`. Applied to tdd `spec:90`, init-lite `spec:87` and spec-panel `spec:120`, and to AC-2.2 `spec:200` ("for tdd, the directory of `<file>`"). WC-11 `spec:69`: "Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file." Workers share the current worktree by default (`CAPS:115`, quoting `[G:placement]` lines 8-11). The spec's own plan is parallel workers per Task (`spec:39`, section 1.3), and section 2.3 `spec:73` says only that the brief states "the output directory"; nothing makes it unique per Task. The spec does see this collision where the directory is fixed (cleanup-audit, `spec:85`: "one audit per worktree runs at a time (WC-11)") but not for file-valued outputs.
- An implementer who follows WC-4 as written writes the contract of `/sc:tdd ... --output docs/tdd/billing.md` to `docs/tdd/return-contract.yaml`. That is wrong because a second tdd worker with `--output docs/tdd/auth.md` writes the same path.
- Concrete attack: state before: no `docs/tdd/return-contract.yaml`. W1 (auth) and W2 (billing) run in one worktree. W2 finishes first: file = `succeeded`, W2 sends `worker_done --report-path docs/tdd/return-contract.yaml`. W1 later fails and overwrites it with `failed`. State after: the coordinator opening W2's reported path reads W1's `failed` contract; the 7.2 step-3 check `--outcome matches the contract's status` (`spec:182`) fails for W2 or passes by accident.
- Recommendation: for a file-valued `--output`, name the contract after the output file (for example `<output-stem>.return-contract.yaml`) or require a unique report directory per Task in the brief (`spec:73`). Priority: High. Quality impact: Correctness of the one artifact the whole design relies on (`spec:62`).

findings.heading: ### B1 [MAJOR, blocking, High priority] WC-4 contract location contradicts file-valued `--output`
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability and ambiguity), Adzic (the concrete example fails), Whittaker (Sentinel Collision: `--output` means a file in some commands and a directory in others).
- Stated texts that contradict each other:
  - `spec:62` (WC-4): "the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)". `spec:73` repeats it: "the output directory, so the report path is known before dispatch".
  - `spec:90` (3.1 tdd): brief must pass "`--output <file>`", report is "the TDD at `--output`".
  - `spec:87` (3.1 init-lite): "`--output <file>`".
  - `spec:120` (3.2 spec-panel): "add `--output`". `spec:108` (explain) and `spec:115` (recommend) say "write ... to a file".
  - `spec:200` (AC-2.2): `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` with step 4 and step 3 reading the WC-4 contract path (`spec:182-183`).
  - Independent corroboration: the command definition under audit says `--output` is file-valued (`command.md:460`: "`--report-dir <dir>` only (`--output` is file-valued)").
- Grading check: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a tdd (or spec-panel, init-lite) that writes its contract to `<the --output file>/return-contract.yaml`. That path sits under a regular file and cannot be created, or collides with the TDD itself. The result is wrong because the one file the coordinator is told to check (`spec:73`, `spec:182`) does not exist, and AC-2.2 and AC-1.2 cannot pass. No guess about the implementer is needed: both texts are in the spec.
- Why it matters: WC-4 is the coordinator's only machine-readable outcome channel (`spec:62`, `spec:182-183`).
- Recommendation: name one rule. Either (a) every command under `--unattended` takes a directory flag (the command's own `--output-dir`, or a new one) and the contract goes there, with `--output <file>` kept as the deliverable path; or (b) for a file-valued `--output`, the contract sits beside it (for example `<dirname(--output)>/return-contract.yaml`). Then restate `spec:73`, `spec:87`, `spec:90`, `spec:120`, `spec:200`. Prefer narrowing the sentence at `spec:62` over adding a mechanism.
- Quality impact: High.

findings.heading: ### B1 [MAJOR, blocking] WC-4 puts the contract in an output directory, but the spec's own tdd brief and acceptance check pass a file
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Adzic.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text builds `/sc:tdd ... --unattended --output <file>` so that it writes `<file>/return-contract.yaml`, because WC-4 says the contract goes in `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, "the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (`SPEC:62`). That is wrong because `<file>` is a file, so the path cannot exist. No contract is written, WC-5 then maps "no report exists" to `--outcome failed` (`SPEC:63`), and AC-2.2 cannot pass.
- Contradicting texts:
  - 3.1 tdd row: brief passes `--output <file>`, report "the TDD at `--output`" (`SPEC:90`, from `INV-B:47,222`).
  - AC-2.2 literally runs `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` and requires "contract `status: blocked` with a non-empty `blocked_question`" (`SPEC:200`).
  - 7.2 step 4 does `test -s <contract>` (`SPEC:183`), with no definition of `<contract>` for a file-valued flag.
  - Section 2.3 tells the coordinator to state "the output directory" in the brief (`SPEC:73`).
  - Several P1/P2 rows say only "add `--output`" or "add a report path" without saying file or directory (`SPEC:99,101,106,108,120`). `spec-panel` is the same case.
- Concrete attack (Whittaker, divergence): at the boundary between a file-valued and a directory-valued output flag, the rule has no branch. State trace: before, brief = `--output out/TDD.md`; after, contract path = `out/TDD.md/return-contract.yaml`, ENOENT/ENOTDIR, report absent, outcome `failed`. The same applies to any P1/P2 command whose new flag is given as a file.
- Recommendation: state in WC-4 where the contract goes when the output flag names a file (for example beside it, or in a separate `--report-dir`), and make the "add `--output`" rows say which kind. Narrow, do not add a mechanism. Priority High.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No blocking architecture finding. Fowler/Newman: the boundary (coordinator plans, command executes, contract file is the only interface) is clean, and R1-R5 (`SPEC:31-37`) are consistent with `CAPS:97-103,145-150`. Hohpe/Nygard concerns are Medium (below).

findings.heading: ### B1 [MAJOR, blocking] WC-4 puts the report in a directory, but tdd's output flag is a file (Wiegers, Adzic, Fowler)
findings.body:
Location: spec:62 (WC-4), spec:90 (tdd row), spec:87 (init-lite row and N-2), spec:200 (AC-2.2), spec:182-183 (7.2 steps 3-4).
Grading check: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a tdd worker that writes its contract to `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where WC-4 defines `<output-dir>` as "the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (spec:62) and the tdd row and AC-2.2 pass `--output <file>` (spec:90, spec:200). The only reading of that text is a directory at the TDD file's own path (for example `docs/auth/TDD_AUTH.md/return-contract.yaml`). That is wrong because the blocked or failed run leaves a directory where the TDD deliverable must be written, so a retry or a happy-path run on the same `--output` cannot create the file, and AC-2.2's own command (`/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>`, spec:200) has no contract path for step 4 of the live check (spec:183, `test -s <contract>`) to open.
Why it holds with no guess: the inventory states the tdd `--output` is a file ("TDD file at `--output`", `INV-B:47`; "the final TDD at `--output` or `docs/[domain]/TDD_[COMPONENT-NAME].md`", `INV-B:222`), and the spec itself treats this case as a defect for init-lite: it adds `--output-dir` because `--output` is file-valued (spec:87, N-2). Nothing in the tdd row (spec:90) does the same.
Same gap, other rows (listed here so the reviser can narrow in one edit; each is graded under B1 only where the contract path is undefined, the rest are in M2): spec-panel "add `--output`" without saying file or directory (spec:120; `INV-B:177-185` (d) says no flag exists today), research "contract naming the generated `claudedocs/research_*.md` path" with no flag for the contract itself (spec:116; `INV-B:131`), index-repo and cleanup-audit, which fix their own output path (`INV-A:53`, `INV-A:42`) yet AC-1.2 (spec:196) passes `--unattended --output <dir>` to every P1 command.
Recommendation: for each command whose existing output flag is file-valued, fixed-path or absent, state in its section-3 row the single flag or fixed path that locates the contract, the way N-2 does for init-lite. Narrow: no new mechanism, one cell per row.
Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability 4 -> 8 for AC-2.2 and AC-1.2.

findings.heading: **B-2 (MAJOR, blocking; Wiegers, Fowler): WC-4's contract location contradicts the file-valued `--output` of several commands and of AC-2.2.**
findings.body:
- Stated texts: WC-4 (SPEC:62) writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is "the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)". Section 3 gives `--output <file>` to tdd (SPEC:90) and init-lite (SPEC:87); the spec-panel, explain and document rows (SPEC:107-108, SPEC:120) also say "add `--output`" or "explicit output" without saying whether it is a file or a directory.
- An implementer who follows WC-4 literally for tdd builds the path `<TDD-file>/return-contract.yaml`, which cannot exist beside the TDD file. AC-2.2 then runs exactly `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` and requires a contract with `status: blocked` (SPEC:200). Step 4 of SPEC:183 runs `test -s <contract>` on a path the spec never defines for file-valued outputs.
- Consequence: the coordinator cannot know the report path "before dispatch" (WC-4's own requirement) for these commands, and AC-2.2 cannot pass as written.
- Recommendation: add one sentence to WC-4 that fixes the contract path when `--output` is a file (for example the file's parent directory, or a named sibling), or make the brief pass a separate directory flag. Priority High.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL as labelled, graded blocking) WC-4 defines the report path as a directory, but the spec's own commands and acceptance check pass a file
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (consistency), Adzic (example), Whittaker (FR-2.2 divergence attack)
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a contract at `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml` where `<output-dir>` is "the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (spec line 62), and X is wrong because for `/sc:tdd` and `/sc:init-lite` the coordinator is told to pass `--output <file>` (spec lines 87, 90), so the path becomes `<file>/return-contract.yaml`, which cannot be created under a regular file, and the spec names no other location.
- Where the texts collide:
  - WC-4 (spec line 62): output dir is a directory; the contract is `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`.
  - 3.1 `tdd` and `init-lite` (spec lines 87, 90): `--output <file>`; their "Report today" is the file itself; no contract row is added for either.
  - AC-2.2 (spec line 200): `/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>` must end with "contract `status: blocked` with a non-empty `blocked_question`". The contract location for this run is stated nowhere, so the check cannot be run as written.
  - Same shape for `spec-panel` (3.2 row, "add `--output`", spec line 120): the command definition in this audit treats `--output` as file-valued (`command.md:460`, "`--output` is file-valued"), so the directory reading of WC-4 does not apply to it either.
- Recommendation: state one rule for where the contract goes when the command's output flag names a file (for example, beside that file), or name a separate directory flag for the contract, and use it in WC-4 and AC-2.2.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: removes the one acceptance check (AC-2.2) that is currently unrunnable for a P2 command.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL, blocking, High priority): the contract path is undefined for file-valued and absent output flags
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (lead), Adzic, Whittaker (Sentinel Collision, FR-2.3).
Texts that conflict:
- WC-4 says the default contract path is `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, "where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)" (spec:62), and the section 3 intro repeats "else `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`" (spec:76).
- The section 3.1 rows say `--output <file>` for tdd (spec:90, report "the TDD at `--output`") and init-lite (spec:87), and the inventory confirms the TDD output is a file path such as `docs/[domain]/TDD_[COMPONENT-NAME].md` (`INV-B:222`). cleanup-audit and index-repo take no output flag in the brief at all (spec:85-86, "none"; `INV-A:42`, `INV-A:53`).
Wrong outcome: an implementer who follows the stated text for tdd builds a contract at `docs/tdd/TDD_AUTH.md/return-contract.yaml` (impossible) or, by taking the parent directory, at `docs/tdd/return-contract.yaml`. Two tdd workers writing into the same `docs/tdd/` then overwrite one contract (breaks WC-11, spec:69). For cleanup-audit and index-repo the text names no directory, so the coordinator cannot "derive that path from the brief" (spec:62). It is wrong because acceptance check AC-2.2 (`/sc:tdd "auth" --unattended --output <file>`, spec:200) and 7.2 step 4 (`test -s <contract>`, spec:183) cannot be run: there is no contract path to test, and `worker_done --report-path` (WC-4) has nothing to carry.
Recommendation (Wiegers): state one rule for file-valued outputs, for example a sibling `<output-file>.return-contract.yaml`, and one named location for the commands with no output flag; add them to the section 3 rows for tdd, init-lite, spec-panel, recommend, explain, cleanup-audit and index-repo.
Quality impact: Completeness +2, Testability +2.
